kjv: Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither
mine: You will not get in here; even the blind and the lame will drive you off
note: Hebrew ki im-hesirkha ha`ivrim wehappischim has "the blind and the lame" as subject of hesir ("turn away, repel"): the Jebusites boast that even their disabled could repel David; the KJV makes David the one who must remove them.

mine: must get up through the water shaft
note: Hebrew tsinnor is a water channel or shaft (probably the city's water tunnel used to get inside); "gutter" suggests a roof drain.
The Hebrew sentence breaks off without a reward clause; the KJV supplies one in italics from the parallel 1 Chr 11:6.

kjv: David and his men burned them
mine: David and his men carried them away
note: The Hebrew has wayyissa'em "and carried them off"; the KJV follows the parallel 1 Chr 14:12, which says David ordered them burned.
Hebrew hasev means "go around"; "fetch a compass" is obsolete English for making a circuit.
Hebrew bekha'im is an unidentified tree or shrub (perhaps balsam or poplar); mulberry is a guess with no support.
